label: Grounding among present concrete things of a history is well-founded
definition: PresentGroundingWellFounded h Concrete grounds holds when, for every history v, the relation 'y and x are concrete and each present at some moment of v, and grounds v y x' is well-founded: there is no endless sequence x0, x1, x2, ... of such things with each x(n+1) grounding x(n). A finite chain of grounds satisfies it. An endless chain of integer-indexed things, each grounded by its predecessor (BegunComingToBe.Control.zeno with its predecessor grounds), violates it.
note: Analyst formulation; attribution deferred. Strictly stronger than PostAbsenceGroundingWellFounded (GroundedBeginnings.postAbsenceOfPresent; strict by GroundedBeginnings.Control.beginningless) and no longer used by the derivation of inert emptiness. An endless per accidens past of generations, which Aquinas grants is not impossible (ST I q.46 a.2 ad 7, STMT-INFINITE-REGRESS-IMPOSSIBLE-ONLY-IN-PER-SE-SERIES), violates it while inert emptiness holds (control 7): that sourced objection targets this strong version, which is why the derivation uses the weak one. Restricted to concrete things present at some moment of the same history: descending chains through abstract, absent or never-present candidates are unconstrained. Not the selected-world ActualGroundingWF of NecessaryRootFork (that ranges over concrete things existing at one world; this ranges over concrete things present at some moment, in every history); neither entails the other without the presence-to-existence contract. Transitivity, asymmetry and irreflexivity are not assumed. Applicability OPEN.
